title: The island where money is giant stones

scenes.say: This is money. Yes, this giant stone! On the island of Yap, in the Pacific, people used huge stone wheels as money. The biggest weighs about as much as a CAR!
But Yap has no stone like this! So people sailed about four hundred kilometres to Palau, carved them by hand, and dragged them home on canoes and rafts. Absolute madness!
So how do you pay with a stone that weighs a tonne? You don't move it! Everyone just agrees it belongs to someone else now. The stone stays. The owner changes!
And the best bit? One stone sank to the bottom of the sea. But everyone agreed it was still down there... so people could STILL spend it! Invisible money!
Sounds crazy? That's literally your bank account! You never see your money. It's just a record everyone trusts. The economist Milton Friedman made exactly this point about Yap!
And Yap still uses the stones today, for big occasions like weddings! Money isn't the stone or the paper. It's a story we all believe. Follow for more!
